items.title: Adobe Commerce RCE Vulnerability (Improper Encoding)
items.summary: This improper encoding vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution over the network without user interaction, potentially leading to full storefront compromise. It affects Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, Magento Open Source, and the Adobe I/O Events extension.

items.title: Adobe Commerce RCE Vulnerability (Unrestricted File Upload)
items.summary: This unrestricted file upload vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by uploading malicious files, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution, session hijacking, and full storefront compromise. It affects Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, Magento Open Source, and the Adobe I/O Events connector.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This security update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, including issues that could lead to arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation. Adobe has also released an isolated patch for these issues.

items.title: Unauthenticated File Upload in Amasty Order Attributes for Magento
items.summary: An unauthenticated arbitrary file upload flaw in the Amasty Order Attributes extension allows attackers to write executable files to a Magento store without logging in, opening the door to remote code execution.

items.title: Critical vulnerability in Mirasvit Cache Warmer for Magento (PHP Object Injection RCE)
items.summary: This unauthenticated PHP object injection vulnerability in Mirasvit Cache Warmer allows remote code execution via a crafted cookie, affecting all versions before 1.11.12. Sansec discovered the flaw on April 24, 2026.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This security update addresses critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, which could lead to arbitrary code execution, arbitrary file system write, application denial-of-service, and security feature bypass.
